title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

target.split: Test = 50% of documents not used as normal training data (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring over test documents

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47|

   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps

  246| text, we first obtain contextualized representations using pre-trained
  247| language models such as BERT [4]. Since tokenizers often split
  248| words into multiple subword units, we need to aggregate subword
  249| embeddings to obtain word-level representations for alignment
  250| with token-level annotations.
  251| While existing approaches always use only the first subword’s
  252| embedding or average pooling across subwords, these methods
  253| may lose critical anomaly signals distributed across different sub-
  254| word positions. To maximize the anomaly signal for each token,
  255| we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings.
  256| Specifically, for a word split into nsubwords with embeddings

  258| etoken = max(e1, e2, . . . , en)

  261| bedding dimension. This aggregation strategy ensures that the

"""Reconnaissance of the released Grammar benchmark files."""
import json
import os
import sys
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data")


def inspect_npy(path):
    print("=" * 70)
    print("NPY:", path, os.path.getsize(path), "bytes")
    obj = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
    print("  dtype:", obj.dtype, "shape:", obj.shape)
    if obj.dtype == object:
        # possibly a dict saved with allow_pickle
        if obj.shape == ():
            d = obj.item()
            print("  scalar object -> type:", type(d))
            if isinstance(d, dict):
                for k, v in d.items():
                    arr = np.asarray(v, dtype=object)
                    print(f"   key={k!r} len={len(v)} shape={arr.shape} first={v[0] if len(v) else None}")
        else:
            print("  first element:", obj.flat[0])
            print("  len:", len(obj))
    else:
        print("  first rows:", obj[:2])
    return obj


def inspect_json(path):
    print("=" * 70)
    print("JSON:", path, os.path.getsize(path), "bytes")
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    print("  top-level type:", type(data), "len:", len(data))
    if isinstance(data, list):
        item = data[0]
        print("  item type:", type(item))
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            print("  keys:", list(item.keys()))
            print("  sample (truncated):")
            s = json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False)
            print("   ", s[:1500])
        # scan key sets across items
        keysets = {}
        for it in data:
            k = tuple(sorted(it.keys())) if isinstance(it, dict) else type(it).__name__
            keysets[k] = keysets.get(k, 0) + 1
        print("  key-set histogram:", keysets)
    return data


if __name__ == "__main__":
    npy = inspect_npy(os.path.join(DATA, "grammar.npy"))
    js = inspect_json(os.path.join(DATA, "grammar_correction_labeled.json"))

"""Deeper look at the grammar annotation arrays + demo notebook code cells."""
import json, os, re, sys
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data")

d = np.load(os.path.join(DATA, "grammar.npy"), allow_pickle=True).item()
sents = [s[0] for s in d["sentences"]]
tokens = d["tokens"]
labels = d["labels"]
print("n docs:", len(sents), len(tokens), len(labels))
print("label types:", set(type(x) for row in labels for x in row))

doc_anom = [int(any(int(x) == 1 for x in row)) for row in labels]
print("anomalous docs (any token==1):", sum(doc_anom))
tot_tok = sum(len(t) for t in tokens)
pos_tok = sum(int(x) for row in labels for x in row)  # if labels are 0/1 ints
print("total tokens:", tot_tok, "anomalous tokens:", pos_tok, "rate:", pos_tok / tot_tok)
lens = [len(t) for t in tokens]
print("doc len min/mean/max:", min(lens), sum(lens) / len(lens), max(lens))

# anomalous docs detail
print("\n--- first 5 anomalous docs ---")
n = 0
for i, row in enumerate(labels):
    if any(int(x) == 1 for x in row):
        print("IDX", i, "SENT:", sents[i])
        print("   TOK:", list(tokens[i]))
        print("   LAB:", [int(x) for x in row])
        n += 1
        if n >= 5:
            break

# does regex tokenization of sentence reproduce tokens?
mismatch = 0
for i, s in enumerate(sents):
    w = re.findall(r"\w+|[^\w\s]", s)
    if w != list(tokens[i]):
        mismatch += 1
        if mismatch <= 3:
            print("MISMATCH", i, s, "| regex:", w, "| gold:", list(tokens[i]))
print("regex-vs-gold token mismatches:", mismatch)

# JSON doc-level labels
with open(os.path.join(DATA, "grammar_correction_labeled.json"), "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    js = json.load(f)
print("\nJSON n:", len(js))
print("data.label values:", sorted(set(item["data"].get("label") for item in js)))
print("data.original_label values:", sorted(set(str(item["data"].get("original_label")) for item in js)))
# alignment between JSON order and npy order
same_text = sum(1 for a, b in zip(js, sents) if a["data"]["text"].replace("\n", "").strip() == b)
print("JSON text == npy sentence (positional):", same_text, "/", len(js))
lab_from_json = [int(item["data"].get("label")) for item in js]
print("doc label agreement json vs npy-derived:", sum(int(a == b) for a, b in zip(lab_from_json, doc_anom)), "/", len(js))

# batching check

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark into a canonical document structure.

Source of truth: repo/data/grammar.npy (written by tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py from
the Label Studio export repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json).

Canonical document:
    {"doc_id": int, "sentence": str, "tokens": [str], "labels": [int], "doc_label": int}

Paper constraints checked here (contract R10 / R11 / R6):
    * 300 documents, 270 normal + 30 anomalous (10% anomaly rate)
    * doc_label == 1 iff at least one token label == 1
    * 50% of the normal documents are used for training; the rest (normal + all
      anomalous) form the test set.
"""
import json
import os

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data")

N_DOCS_EXPECTED = 300
N_NORMAL_EXPECTED = 270
N_ANOMALOUS_EXPECTED = 30


def load_grammar_docs(data_dir=DATA_DIR, verbose=True):
    """Return the list of 300 grammar documents (deterministic file order)."""
    npy_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "grammar.npy")
    obj = np.load(npy_path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    sentences = [s[0] if isinstance(s, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)) else s for s in obj["sentences"]]
    tokens = [list(t) for t in obj["tokens"]]
    labels = [[int(x) for x in l] for l in obj["labels"]]

    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(sentences, tokens, labels)):
        assert len(toks) == len(labs), f"doc {i}: {len(toks)} tokens vs {len(labs)} labels"
        assert set(labs) <= {0, 1}, f"doc {i}: labels outside {{0,1}}: {set(labs)}"
        doc_label = 1 if any(l == 1 for l in labs) else 0
        docs.append({"doc_id": i, "sentence": sent, "tokens": toks,
                     "labels": labs, "doc_label": doc_label})
    _validate(docs, verbose=verbose)
    return docs


def _validate(docs, verbose=True):
    n = len(docs)
    n_anom = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    n_norm = n - n_anom
    assert n == N_DOCS_EXPECTED, f"expected {N_DOCS_EXPECTED} documents, got {n}"
    assert n_norm == N_NORMAL_EXPECTED, f"expected {N_NORMAL_EXPECTED} normal docs, got {n_norm}"
    assert n_anom == N_ANOMALOUS_EXPECTED, f"expected {N_ANOMALOUS_EXPECTED} anomalous docs, got {n_anom}"
    # R11: doc label consistent with token labels (also vs the raw Label Studio export)
    for d in docs:
        assert d["doc_label"] == (1 if any(l == 1 for l in d["labels"]) else 0)
    js_path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "grammar_correction_labeled.json")
    if os.path.exists(js_path):
        with open(js_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            js = json.load(f)
        assert len(js) == n
        for item, d in zip(js, docs):
            assert item["data"]["text"].replace("\n", "").strip() == d["sentence"], d["doc_id"]
            assert int(item["data"]["label"]) == d["doc_label"], d["doc_id"]
    if verbose:
        tot_tok = sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in docs)
        pos_tok = sum(sum(d["labels"]) for d in docs)
        print(f"[data_grammar] docs={n} normal={n_norm} anomalous={n_anom} "
              f"rate={n_anom / n:.3f} tokens={tot_tok} anomalous_tokens={pos_tok} "
              f"token_rate={pos_tok / tot_tok:.4f}")


def split_docs(docs, seed=0, train_frac=0.5, smoke=False):
    """50% of the normal documents -> training (memory bank); the rest + all
    anomalous documents -> test (paper Sec. 6.1, contract R6).

    Returns (train_docs, test_docs). Deterministic in `seed`.
    """
    normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anomalous = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    if smoke:
        # keep both classes on both sides with a tiny subset
        normal_sel, anom_sel = normal[:8], anomalous[:2]
        n_train = max(1, int(round(len(normal_sel) * train_frac)))
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        idx = rng.permutation(len(normal_sel))
        train = [normal_sel[i] for i in idx[:n_train]]
        test = [normal_sel[i] for i in idx[n_train:]] + list(anom_sel)
        return train, test

    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    idx = rng.permutation(len(normal))
    n_train = int(round(len(normal) * train_frac))
    train = [normal[i] for i in idx[:n_train]]
    test = [normal[i] for i in idx[n_train:]] + anomalous
    assert all(d["doc_label"] == 0 for d in train), "training set must contain no anomalies (R3)"
    assert len(train) == n_train
    assert len(train) + len(test) == len(docs)
    return train, test


if __name__ == "__main__":
    docs = load_grammar_docs()
    for seed in (0, 1, 2):
        tr, te = split_docs(docs, seed=seed)
        n_tok_tr = sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in tr)
        n_tok_te = sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in te)
        pos_te = sum(sum(d["labels"]) for d in te)
        print(f"seed={seed}: train_docs={len(tr)} train_tokens={n_tok_tr} | "
              f"test_docs={len(te)} test_tokens={n_tok_te} test_pos_tokens={pos_te} "
              f"test_doc_anom={sum(d['doc_label'] for d in te)}")
    tr, te = split_docs(docs, seed=0, smoke=True)
    print("smoke: train", len(tr), "test", len(te))

"""Recover eval.split_anomaly_data's behaviour from the frozen Demo.ipynb outputs.

texts against the .npy document order tells us whether the split is sequential or shuffled,
and how many documents land on each side.
"""
import json, os, re
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data")
nb = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "demo.ipynb"), "r", encoding="utf-8"))

d = np.load(os.path.join(DATA, "restaurant_review.npy"), allow_pickle=True).item()
sents = [s[0] for s in d["sentences"]]
labels = [[int(x) for x in l] for l in d["labels"]]
doc_anom = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]
print("restaurant_review: n=", len(sents), "anomalous docs=", sum(doc_anom))
anom_idx = [i for i, v in enumerate(doc_anom) if v]
print("anomalous doc indices: first 10:", anom_idx[:10], "last 10:", anom_idx[-10:])
print("normal doc indices range:", 0, "to", max(i for i, v in enumerate(doc_anom) if not v))


def sentences_from_cell(idx):
    out = []
    for o in nb["cells"][idx].get("outputs", []):
        if o.get("output_type") == "stream":
            t = "".join(o.get("text", []))
            out = re.findall(r"Sentence \d+/\d+: (.*)", t)
    return out


train_sents = sentences_from_cell(2)
test_sents = sentences_from_cell(3)
print("\nn train sentences in notebook:", len(train_sents), " n test:", len(test_sents))


def match(seq, name):
    pos = []
    for s in seq:
        hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(sents) if t.strip() == s.strip()]
        pos.append(hits[0] if len(hits) >= 1 else None)
    none_ct = sum(p is None for p in pos)
    print(f"{name}: matched {len(pos) - none_ct}/{len(pos)}  first 10 idx: {pos[:10]}  last 10 idx: {pos[-10:]}")
    monotone = all(a <= b for a, b in zip([p for p in pos if p is not None], [p for p in pos if p is not None][1:]))
    print(f"   monotone increasing? {monotone}")
    return pos


# only compare the first 30 and last 30 to keep it cheap
p_train = match(train_sents[:30] + train_sents[-30:], "TRAIN(head+tail)")
p_test = match(test_sents[:30] + test_sents[-30:], "TEST(head+tail)")

# check the full test set head: is test = second half of the file?

print("npy[0]:", sents[0][:80])
print("notebook test[0]:", test_sents[0][:80])

print("npy[525]:", sents[525][:80])
print("notebook train[-1]:", train_sents[-1][:80])
print("notebook test[-1]:", test_sents[-1][:80])

"""Time the authors' align.extract_word_embeddings on CPU for a subset of Grammar docs."""
import contextlib, io, os, sys, time
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "repo"))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar_docs
from align import extract_word_embeddings
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")
model.eval()
import torch
torch.set_num_threads(4)

sub = docs[:20]
t0 = time.time()
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    res = extract_word_embeddings(model=model, tokenizer=tok,
                                  all_tokens=[d["tokens"] for d in sub],
                                  all_labels=[d["labels"] for d in sub],
                                  model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu")
dt = time.time() - t0
print(f"align.py on 20 docs: {dt:.2f}s -> {dt/20*300:.1f}s for 300 docs (4 threads)")
print("units per doc:", [len(r) for r in res])
print("tokens per doc:", [len(d['tokens']) for d in sub])
print("embedding shape:", res[0][0]["embedding"].shape, res[0][0]["embedding"].dtype)
print("labels:", res[0][0]["label"], "token:", res[0][0]["token"])

# 8 threads
torch.set_num_threads(8)
t0 = time.time()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    res2 = extract_word_embeddings(model=model, tokenizer=tok,
                                   all_tokens=[d["tokens"] for d in sub],
                                   all_labels=[d["labels"] for d in sub],
                                   model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu")
print(f"with 8 threads: {time.time()-t0:.2f}s")
print("max-abs diff vs 4 threads:", float(np.max(np.abs(res[0][0]['embedding'] - res2[0][0]['embedding']))))

"""BERT-base-uncased word-level embedding extraction with element-wise max pooling.

Implements paper Eq. (1): e_token = max(e_1, ..., e_n) over the subword vectors of a word,
using the last hidden state of BERT-base-uncased, skipping [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] (word_idx None).

This is a batched, print-free re-implementation of the authors' repo/align.py
extract_word_embeddings(); src/check_align_parity.py asserts the two agree numerically.
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import torch

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-uncased"
MAX_LENGTH = 128
BATCH_SIZE = 32


def _load(model_name=MODEL_NAME):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model.eval()
    return tok, model


def embed_documents(docs, tok=None, model=None, model_name=MODEL_NAME,
                    batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, max_length=MAX_LENGTH, num_threads=8,
                    verbose=True):
    """Embed every document and return per-word units.

    docs: list of dicts with "tokens" (gold word list) and "labels".
    Returns list of dicts:
        {"doc_id", "units": [{"token", "label", "emb"} ...]}  (one unit per gold token)
    """
    if tok is None or model is None:
        tok, model = _load(model_name)
    torch.set_num_threads(num_threads)

    out = []
    n = len(docs)
    for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
        chunk = docs[start:start + batch_size]
        encodings = [
            tok(d["tokens"], is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                padding=False, max_length=max_length, add_special_tokens=True)
            for d in chunk
        ]
        ids = [e["input_ids"] for e in encodings]
        padded = tok.pad({"input_ids": ids}, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)
        input_ids = padded["input_ids"]
        attention_mask = padded["attention_mask"]
        with torch.no_grad():
            hidden = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state
        hidden = hidden.float().cpu().numpy()

        for k, d in enumerate(chunk):
            word_ids = encodings[k].word_ids(batch_index=0)
            vecs = hidden[k]
            units = []
            prev = None
            cur = []
            cur_tok = None
            cur_lab = None

            def flush():
                if cur:
                    units.append({"token": cur_tok, "label": cur_lab,
                                  "emb": np.max(np.stack(cur), axis=0)})

            for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                if wid is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / padding
                if wid != prev:
                    flush()
                    cur_tok = d["tokens"][wid]
                    cur_lab = int(d["labels"][wid])
                    cur = [vecs[pos]]
                else:
                    cur.append(vecs[pos])
                prev = wid
            flush()
            if len(units) != len(d["tokens"]):
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"alignment loss in doc {d['doc_id']}: {len(units)} units vs "
                    f"{len(d['tokens'])} gold tokens (truncation at max_length={max_length}?)")
            out.append({"doc_id": d["doc_id"], "units": units})
        if verbose:
            print(f"\r[embed] {min(start + batch_size, n)}/{n} docs", end="", flush=True)
    if verbose:
        print()
    return out


def units_to_matrix(embedded, doc_ids=None):
    """Flatten embedded docs into (X, y, doc_index) arrays."""
    X, y, didx = [], [], []
    for di, doc in enumerate(embedded):
        if doc_ids is not None and doc["doc_id"] not in doc_ids:
            continue
        for u in doc["units"]:
            X.append(u["emb"])
            y.append(int(u["label"]))
            didx.append(di)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64), np.asarray(y, dtype=np.int64), np.asarray(didx, dtype=np.int64)

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py (contract R3 / R4).

TokenCore.fit(X) builds the memory bank from X (here: word-level embeddings of the tokens of
the normal training documents only -> R3) and TokenCore.decision_function(X) returns the
nearest-neighbour distance of each row of X to the bank (Eq. 2 -> R4, larger = more anomalous).
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
REPO = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo")
if REPO not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO)

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' file, unmodified)


def fit_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1, aggregation="max"):
    """Fit the memory bank on X_train, return per-row anomaly scores for X_test."""
    X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float64)
    X_test = np.asarray(X_test, dtype=np.float64)
    if X_train.ndim != 2 or X_test.ndim != 2:
        raise RuntimeError(f"expected 2-D embedding matrices, got {X_train.shape} / {X_test.shape}")
    if X_train.shape[1] != X_test.shape[1]:
        raise RuntimeError(f"embedding width mismatch: {X_train.shape} vs {X_test.shape}")
    if not np.isfinite(X_train).all() or not np.isfinite(X_test).all():
        raise RuntimeError("non-finite embeddings")
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, aggregation=aggregation)
    model.fit(X_train)
    if getattr(model, "memory_bank", None) is None or len(model.memory_bank) != len(X_train):
        raise RuntimeError("memory bank does not contain every normal-training token")
    scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    if len(scores) != len(X_test) or not np.isfinite(scores).all():
        raise RuntimeError(f"bad scores: n={len(scores)} vs {len(X_test)}")
    return scores, model

import json, os, re
from collections import defaultdict
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data")
nb = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "demo.ipynb"), "r", encoding="utf-8"))


def cell_sentences(idx):
    for o in nb["cells"][idx].get("outputs", []):
        if o.get("output_type") == "stream":
            return re.findall(r"Sentence \d+/\d+: (.*)", "".join(o.get("text", [])))
    return []


def split(docs_tokens, doc_anom, seed=42):
    n_total = len(docs_tokens)
    normal = [i for i, a in enumerate(doc_anom) if a == 0]
    anom = [i for i, a in enumerate(doc_anom) if a == 1]
    idx = np.random.RandomState(seed).permutation(len(normal))
    n_train = n_total // 2
    return [normal[i] for i in idx[:n_train]], [normal[i] for i in idx[n_train:]] + anom


tr_txt, te_txt = cell_sentences(2), cell_sentences(3)

occ = defaultdict(list)

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce Table 1 (TokenCore row) of "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection"
(arXiv:2601.13644) on the Grammar benchmark.

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 / 6.1, contract R1-R7, R9-R11):
  1. data_grammar  : released 300-document Grammar corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous)
  2. split_docs    : train = n_total//2 normal documents (memory bank), test = the rest
                     + all anomalous documents           (R6)
  3. embed_bert    : BERT-base-uncased last hidden state, element-wise max pooling of the
                     subwords of each word into one word-level vector  (R1, R2, R9)
  4. detector      : the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py - memory bank of the normal
                     training token embeddings, score = nearest-neighbour Euclidean
                     distance (R3, R4, Eq. 1-2)
  5. evaluate      : token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens, document-level
                     scores by the mean of the token scores (R5, Eq. 3) and R7.

Writes results/metrics.json.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar_docs, split_docs      # noqa: E402
from src.embed_bert import embed_documents, units_to_matrix, MODEL_NAME  # noqa: E402
from src.detector import fit_score                              # noqa: E402
from src import evaluate                                        # noqa: E402

RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
TARGET_CLAIM = "C1"


def run_once(docs, embedded, train, test, verbose=True):
    """Memory bank from the training tokens, score the test tokens, return metrics."""
    X_tr, y_tr, _ = units_to_matrix(embedded, doc_ids={d["doc_id"] for d in train})
    X_te, y_te, doc_idx_te = units_to_matrix(embedded, doc_ids={d["doc_id"] for d in test})
    assert y_tr.sum() == 0, "memory bank must contain no anomalous tokens (R3)"
    assert X_tr.shape[1] == 768, f"BERT-base-uncased width expected, got {X_tr.shape}"

    doc_labels = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in test])
    scores, model = fit_score(X_tr, X_te)

    tok = evaluate.token_metrics(y_te, scores)
    dscr = evaluate.document_scores(scores, doc_idx_te, n_docs=len(test))
    doc = evaluate.document_metrics(dscr, doc_labels)
    ctrl = evaluate.random_control(y_te, doc_idx_te, doc_labels, seed=0)

    if verbose:
        print(f"    bank={X_tr.shape[0]} tokens ({X_tr.shape[1]}-d) | "
              f"test={X_te.shape[0]} tokens, {int(y_te.sum())} anomalous "
              f"({y_te.mean():.4f}) | token AUROC={tok['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={tok['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"doc AUROC={doc['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={doc['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"random-control token AUROC={ctrl['token']['auroc']:.4f}")
    return {
        "token_auroc": tok["auroc"], "token_auprc": tok["auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc["auroc"], "doc_auprc": doc["auprc"],
        "random_control": ctrl,
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_tr.shape[0]), "n_test_tokens": int(X_te.shape[0]),
        "n_pos_tokens": int(y_te.sum()), "n_test_docs": int(len(test)),
        "n_test_anom_docs": int(doc_labels.sum()),
        "score_min": float(np.min(scores)), "score_max": float(np.max(scores)),
        "score_mean": float(np.mean(scores)),
    }


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--datasets", default="grammar")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42, help="primary split seed")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="42,0,1,2", help="comma list for the spread")
    ap.add_argument("--mode", default="notebook", choices=["notebook", "paper"],
                    help="split rule: |train| = n_total//2 (authors' demo) or 50% of the "
                         "normal pool (literal Sec. 6.1 wording)")
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="10-document subset, end-to-end only")
    ap.add_argument("--num-threads", type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    assert args.datasets == "grammar", "only the Grammar benchmark is wired up for C1"
    t_start = time.time()
    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    evaluate.self_check()

    print("[1] load Grammar benchmark")

"""Parity check: my batched max-pooling extractor (src/embed_bert.py) vs the authors'
repo/align.py extract_word_embeddings (unmodified), on ~20 Grammar documents.

Run:  python -m src.check_align_parity   (from the workspace root)
Asserts max |difference| < 1e-4 per element and identical labels/token order.
"""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
for p in (ROOT, os.path.join(ROOT, "repo")):
    if p not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, p)

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar_docs          # noqa: E402
from src.embed_bert import embed_documents              # noqa: E402
from align import extract_word_embeddings               # noqa: E402  (authors' file)

MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"


def main():
    docs = load_grammar_docs(verbose=False)
    sub = docs[:16] + docs[270:274]          # 16 normal + 4 anomalous
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(MODEL)
    model.eval()
    torch.set_num_threads(4)

    t0 = time.time()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        ref = extract_word_embeddings(model=model, tokenizer=tok,
                                      all_tokens=[d["tokens"] for d in sub],
                                      all_labels=[d["labels"] for d in sub],
                                      model_name=MODEL, device="cpu")
    t_ref = time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    mine = embed_documents(sub, tok=tok, model=model, verbose=False)
    t_mine = time.time() - t0

    ref_emb = np.array([u["embedding"] for s in ref for u in s], dtype=np.float64)
    ref_lab = np.array([int(u["label"]) for s in ref for u in s])
    ref_tok = [u["token"] for s in ref for u in s]
    my_emb = np.array([u["emb"] for d in mine for u in d["units"]], dtype=np.float64)
    my_lab = np.array([u["label"] for d in mine for u in d["units"]])
    my_tok = [u["token"] for d in mine for u in d["units"]]

    print(f"units: authors={ref_emb.shape} mine={my_emb.shape}")
    print(f"time: authors (per-doc loop, logging) {t_ref:.1f}s | mine (batched) {t_mine:.1f}s "
          f"-> {t_ref / max(t_mine, 1e-6):.1f}x faster")
    assert ref_emb.shape == my_emb.shape, (ref_emb.shape, my_emb.shape)
    assert ref_lab.tolist() == my_lab.tolist(), "label mismatch"
    assert ref_tok == my_tok, "token order mismatch"
    diff = np.abs(ref_emb - my_emb).max()
    print(f"max |align.py - embed_bert.py| = {diff:.3e}")
    assert diff < 1e-4, diff
    print("PARITY OK: element-wise max pooling over subwords, last hidden state, "
          "special tokens skipped - identical to the authors' align.py")

    # hand-checked example of Eq. (1): coordinate-wise max of the subword vectors

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce Table 1 (TokenCore row) of "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection"
(arXiv:2601.13644) on the Grammar benchmark -> claims C1 (token AUROC) and C2 (token AUPRC),
with the Grammar document-level numbers (Eq. 3) as by-products.

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 / 6.1, contract R1-R7, R9-R11):
  1. data_grammar  : released 300-document Grammar corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10)
  2. split_docs    : train = normal documents only (memory bank), test = the remaining
                     normal documents + all anomalous documents            (R6)
  3. embed_bert    : BERT-base-uncased last hidden state, element-wise max pooling of the
                     subwords of each word into one word-level vector       (R1, R2, R9)
                     (numerically identical to the authors' repo/align.py - see
                      src/check_align_parity.py)
  4. detector      : the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py - memory bank built from the
                     normal training token embeddings (R3), score = nearest-neighbour
                     Euclidean distance to the bank (R4, Eq. 2)
  5. evaluate      : token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (as in the authors'
                     Demo.ipynb), document-level score = mean of the token scores of a
                     document (R5, Eq. 3), plus a random-score control        (R7)

Writes results/metrics.json.  No paper result value is hard-coded anywhere: every number in
the output is computed here from the released data.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar_docs, split_docs              # noqa: E402
from src.embed_bert import embed_documents, units_to_matrix, MODEL_NAME  # noqa: E402
from src.detector import fit_score                                       # noqa: E402
from src import evaluate                                                 # noqa: E402

RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")


def run_once(emb_by_id, train, test, verbose=True, tag=""):
    """Memory bank from the training tokens, nearest-neighbour score the test tokens, metrics."""
    embedded_train = [emb_by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in train]
    embedded_test = [emb_by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in test]
    X_tr, y_tr, _ = units_to_matrix(embedded_train)
    # doc_idx indexes into `test`, so document scores line up 1:1 with doc_labels
    X_te, y_te, doc_idx_te = units_to_matrix(embedded_test)
    assert y_tr.sum() == 0, "memory bank must contain no anomalous tokens (R3)"
    assert X_tr.shape[1] == 768, f"BERT-base-uncased width expected, got {X_tr.shape}"
    assert doc_idx_te.min() == 0 and doc_idx_te.max() == len(test) - 1
    assert len(y_te) == sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in test)

    doc_labels = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in test])
    scores, _model = fit_score(X_tr, X_te)

    tok = evaluate.token_metrics(y_te, scores)
    dscr = evaluate.document_scores(scores, doc_idx_te, n_docs=len(test))
    doc = evaluate.document_metrics(dscr, doc_labels)
    ctrl = evaluate.random_control(y_te, doc_idx_te, doc_labels, seed=0)

    if verbose:
        print(f"    {tag} bank={X_tr.shape[0]} tokens ({X_tr.shape[1]}-d) | "
              f"test={X_te.shape[0]} tokens, {int(y_te.sum())} anomalous ({y_te.mean():.4f}) | "
              f"token AUROC={tok['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={tok['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"doc AUROC={doc['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={doc['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"random-control token AUROC={ctrl['token']['auroc']:.4f}")
    return {
        "token_auroc": tok["auroc"], "token_auprc": tok["auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc["auroc"], "doc_auprc": doc["auprc"],
        "random_control": ctrl,
        "n_train_docs": len(train), "n_test_docs": len(test),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_tr.shape[0]), "n_test_tokens": int(X_te.shape[0]),
        "n_pos_tokens": int(y_te.sum()), "n_test_anom_docs": int(doc_labels.sum()),
        "score_mean": float(np.mean(scores)), "score_max": float(np.max(scores)),
    }


def sweep(emb_by_id, docs, seeds, mode, label):
    res = {}
    for s in seeds:
        tr, te = split_docs(docs, seed=s, mode=mode, verbose=False)
        res[s] = run_once(emb_by_id, tr, te, tag=f"[{label} mode={mode} seed={s}]")
    vals = [res[s]["token_auroc"] for s in seeds]
    print(f"  -> {label}/{mode}: token AUROC {np.mean(vals):.4f} +- {np.std(vals):.4f} "
          f"(seeds {seeds})")
    return res, {"mean": float(np.mean(vals)), "std": float(np.std(vals)),
                 "min": float(np.min(vals)), "max": float(np.max(vals))}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--datasets", default="grammar")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42, help="primary split seed")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="42,0,1,2", help="comma list for the spread")
    ap.add_argument("--mode", default="notebook", choices=["notebook", "paper"],
                    help="primary split rule (see src/data_grammar.split_docs)")
    ap.add_argument("--both-modes", action="store_true", default=True,
                    help="also report the other split rule")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL_NAME)
    ap.add_argument("--sensitivity-model", default="bert-base-cased",
                    help="embedding backbone used for the sensitivity block "
                         "(the authors' Demo.ipynb ran bert-base-cased; the paper text says "
                         "BERT-base-uncased, which is what the primary number uses)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-sensitivity", dest="sensitivity", action="store_false", default=True)
    ap.add_argument("--num-threads", type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="10-document subset, end-to-end only")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    assert args.datasets == "grammar", "only the Grammar benchmark is wired up for C1"

def read_target_from_state():
    """Parse the claim target and tolerance from the workspace contract files.

    The number is never hard-coded in this script: it is read from
    state/plan.json (config.target_value, e.g. "0.6371 token AUROC (C1)") and
    state/claim_contract.json (tolerance.value), and only echoed into the output
    as context next to the value our code actually computed.
    """
    target, tol, claim = None, None, None
    try:
        plan = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "state", "plan.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
        import re
        txt = str(plan.get("config", {}).get("target_value", ""))
        m = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)", txt)
        target = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
        m = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)", str(plan.get("config", {}).get("tolerance", "")))
        tol = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    except Exception as exc:
        print("  (could not read target from state/plan.json:", exc, ")")
    try:
        c = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "state", "claim_contract.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
        claim = c.get("match_target", {}).get("claim_id")
        tol = float(c.get("tolerance", {}).get("value", tol)) if c.get("tolerance") else tol
    except Exception as exc:
        print("  (could not read tolerance from state/claim_contract.json:", exc, ")")
    return target, tol, claim

def run_once(emb_by_id, train, test, verbose=True, tag=""):
    """Memory bank from the training tokens, nearest-neighbour score the test tokens, metrics."""
    embedded_train = [emb_by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in train]
    embedded_test = [emb_by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in test]
    X_tr, y_tr, _ = units_to_matrix(embedded_train)
    # doc_idx indexes into `test`, so document scores line up 1:1 with doc_labels
    X_te, y_te, doc_idx_te = units_to_matrix(embedded_test)
    assert y_tr.sum() == 0, "memory bank must contain no anomalous tokens (R3)"
    assert X_tr.shape[1] == 768, f"BERT-base-uncased width expected, got {X_tr.shape}"
    assert doc_idx_te.min() == 0 and doc_idx_te.max() == len(test) - 1
    assert len(y_te) == sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in test)

    doc_labels = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in test])
    scores, _model = fit_score(X_tr, X_te)

    tok = evaluate.token_metrics(y_te, scores)
    dscr = evaluate.document_scores(scores, doc_idx_te, n_docs=len(test))
    doc = evaluate.document_metrics(dscr, doc_labels)
    ctrl = evaluate.random_control(y_te, doc_idx_te, doc_labels, seed=0)

    if verbose:
        print(f"    {tag} bank={X_tr.shape[0]} tokens ({X_tr.shape[1]}-d) | "
              f"test={X_te.shape[0]} tokens, {int(y_te.sum())} anomalous ({y_te.mean():.4f}) | "
              f"token AUROC={tok['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={tok['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"doc AUROC={doc['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={doc['auprc']:.4f} | "
              f"random-control token AUROC={ctrl['token']['auroc']:.4f}")
    return {
        "token_auroc": tok["auroc"], "token_auprc": tok["auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc["auroc"], "doc_auprc": doc["auprc"],
        "random_control": ctrl,
        "n_train_docs": len(train), "n_test_docs": len(test),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_tr.shape[0]), "n_test_tokens": int(X_te.shape[0]),
        "n_pos_tokens": int(y_te.sum()), "n_test_anom_docs": int(doc_labels.sum()),
        "score_mean": float(np.mean(scores)), "score_max": float(np.max(scores)),
    }

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The clean rerun computes Grammar token-level AUROC from scratch: 0.6137 at seed 42 with bert-base-uncased, a gap of -0.0234 versus the 0.6371 target, outside the ±0.02 tolerance; the 4-seed uncased mean is 0.5998 ± 0.0248. Core TokenCore fidelity is strong: authors' TokenCore.py is used unmodified for the normal-only memory bank and 1-NN Euclidean token scoring, embeddings use element-wise max pooling over WordPiece subwords, document scores use mean aggregation, and sklearn AUROC/AUPRC parity is checked; no metric value is hard-coded. The largest caveat is the backbone conflict: the cased sensitivity block gives 0.6324 at seed 42 and 0.6374 ± 0.0291 over four seeds, matching all four Grammar Table-1 cells, while the contract/paper-text primary uses uncased. The primary split is the recovered notebook-style split with 150 normal training documents rather than the literal 50%-of-normal 135; the alternative paper-style split gives 0.6143 at seed 42. Baselines and the other datasets are not run, so R8 is missing, but the C1 target experiment itself is not scaled down or substituted.

requirement_check.evidence: Primary TokenCore run uses bert-base-uncased and element-wise max pooling as required, but the six baselines that R1 says must share this front-end are not run; only a cased TokenCore sensitivity block is added.
src/embed_bert.py groups WordPiece subwords by word_ids and applies np.max over their last-hidden-state vectors; the separate alignment-parity command against the authors' align.py exited 0.
The memory bank is built only from training-document tokens; metrics.json reports n_pos_tokens_in_bank=0 for every seed and bank size equal to the training-token count (1327/1342/1357/1351).
src/detector.py imports the authors' unmodified TokenCore, fits the bank on training tokens, and scores test tokens with n_neighbors=1 nearest-neighbour distance.
src/evaluate.py document_scores implements the arithmetic mean of token scores per document; its self-check verifies [1,3,5,7] -> [2,6].

The primary mode=notebook split trains on n_total//2 = 150 normal Grammar documents, not 50% of the 270-normal pool (135); the literal paper-style 135/165 split is computed only as an alternative mode in metrics.json.
metrics.json reports token AUROC/AUPRC and document AUROC/AUPRC for TokenCore; metric parity against sklearn is reported with max_abs_diff=0.0.
No LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder, or LUNAR runs or comparison table are present; only TokenCore metrics are computed.
Subword units are aggregated to exactly one vector per gold word token, and the code asserts len(units)==len(gold tokens) per document.
metrics.json counts 300 documents, 270 normal, 30 anomalous, anomaly rate 0.1, 2746 total tokens, and 47 anomalous tokens.
src/data_grammar.py sets doc_label = 1 iff any token label is 1 and validates this against the released grammar_correction_labeled.json.

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A12/A13/A14/A15: split rule/seed and cased-vs-uncased backbone conflict between the paper text and the authors' released Demo.ipynb)
randomness (4-seed token-AUROC std 0.0248; seed 42 at 0.6137 is below the 4-seed mean 0.5998 for uncased, and cased gives 0.6374 mean)
